tagline: Sync personal Todoist tasks to team Trello boards without manual copying
metaTitle: Trello Todoist Integration: Sync Cards and Tasks Both Ways
metaDescription: Publish Todoist tasks as Trello cards and pull assigned cards into Todoist, with completion kept in sync. GAIA updates client boards. See the setup steps.
intro:
Trello's visual Kanban boards are a team staple for tracking shared work, but many individuals prefer Todoist's list-based interface for their own task management. The problem is that work captured privately there rarely makes it onto the team board in a timely way, creating gaps between what you've committed to and what your team can see.

GAIA connects the two so that tasks flow between them automatically. When a Todoist task is ready to share with the team, GAIA can create a Trello card in the right board and list, complete with description, due date, and labels. When a card is assigned to you, GAIA can pull it into your personal inbox for tracking. Completions and archive actions propagate both ways so neither side falls out of date.

This suits small teams who use the shared board as their project view but allow individuals to use their preferred personal tools, and freelancers who manage their own work privately but share progress with clients on a board.

useCases.title: Publish Todoist tasks as Trello cards
useCases.description: When a task is ready for team visibility, GAIA creates a corresponding card on the designated board and list, carrying across the title, description, due date, and any relevant labels.

useCases.title: Pull assigned Trello cards into Todoist
useCases.description: GAIA watches for cards assigned to you and adds them to your inbox with due dates and priority so your daily review stays centralized in your preferred app.

useCases.title: Keep completion status synchronized
useCases.description: Checking off a task archives the linked card, and moving a card to Done marks the task complete, so both views stay accurate without manual housekeeping.

useCases.title: Client project board updates
useCases.description: Freelancers can capture work during the day and let GAIA push completed items to a client-facing board each evening, giving clients visibility without requiring a change in personal workflow.

useCases.title: Meeting action items to Kanban cards
useCases.description: Action items captured during a meeting are automatically distributed to the right boards and assigned to the right team members, turning meeting notes into trackable Kanban cards.

howItWorks.step: Connect Todoist and Trello to GAIA
howItWorks.description: Authenticate both accounts in GAIA's integration settings using OAuth. GAIA only requests access to the boards and projects you specify, keeping unrelated data private.

howItWorks.step: Map projects to boards and lists
howItWorks.description: Tell GAIA which projects should sync to which boards, and which list newly promoted tasks should land in. You can define different mappings for different teams or clients.

howItWorks.step: GAIA handles card creation and status sync automatically
howItWorks.description: GAIA monitors both sides continuously, creating and updating cards and tasks as changes occur. You can also trigger one-off syncs or ask GAIA to report on items that exist in one tool but not the other.

faqs.question: Can GAIA sync Trello checklist items to Todoist sub-tasks?
faqs.answer: Yes. GAIA can map checklist items to sub-tasks when creating linked records. Changes to checklist completion status on a card propagate to the corresponding sub-tasks and vice versa.

faqs.question: What happens to attachments on cards?
faqs.answer: GAIA includes links to card attachments in the corresponding task description. Uploading files directly to a task and pushing them to the card as attachments is also supported for common file types.

faqs.question: Can I share a board with a client without giving them access to my personal task list?
faqs.answer: Yes. GAIA acts as the bridge between your private task list and the shared board. Clients only see the board you've shared with them; your personal task list remains entirely private.
